title: Development and validation of a multiplex fluorescent microsphere immunoassay assay for detection of porcine cytokines
author: Hall, Ison, et al.
materials: For each cytokine, the relevant capture antibody was coupled following manufacturer’s instructions, using reagents from the Bio-Plex amine coupling kit (Bio-Rad, UK) except where specified. All reagents were brought to room temperature (RT) before use. Briefly, 100 μl (1.25 × 106 microspheres) of fluorescently distinct microspheres (beads) were separated from the supernatant using a magnetic separator and washed in 100 μl bead wash buffer by vortexing for 30 seconds (s). The supernatant was removed by magnetic separation again and then the washed beads were resuspended in 80 μl of bead activation buffer by vortexing for 30 s. To this, 10 μl of S-NHS (50 mg/ml; Fisher, UK) and 10 μl of EDC (50 mg/ml; Fisher, UK) prepared in bead activation buffer were added and mixed gently by vortexing. The tube was incubated in the dark with shaking for 20 min at room temperature (RT). After incubation, 100 μl phosphate buffered saline (PBS; pH 7.4) was added and vortexed for 10 s. The supernatant was removed by magnetic separation and the PBS wash step repeated. The beads were then resuspended in 100 μl PBS and vortexed for 30 s. The recombinant cytokine protein was added to the activated beads and mixed by vortexing and then incubated for 2 h in the dark at RT with shaking.

The supernatant was removed by magnetic separation, using a MagRack 6 (GE Healthcare) and coupled beads were resuspended in 500 μl PBS. The supernatant was again removed, and beads were resuspended in 250 μl of blocking buffer, vortexed for 15 s. and incubated in the dark at RT for 30 min with shaking. The supernatant was removed by magnetic separation and beads were resuspended in 500 μl of storage buffer. Further concentration of the beads was obtained when the supernatant was removed by magnetic separation and then coupled beads were resuspended in 150 μl of storage buffer. The bead concentration was determined using an automated cell counter (TC10 Bio-Rad, UK). The coupled beads were stored in the dark at 2–8 °C until use.

Capture and detection antibodies and recombinant cytokines were purchased as matched pairs if available which were commercially validated for binding to different epitopes on the antigen (Table 1). This increased the likelihood of antibody reactivity for each cytokine and decreased likelihood of cross-reactivity with other cytokines. Individual cytokine measurements were initially optimised as a singleplex for IL-1β, IL-4 IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TNF-α) before combining them to perform a multiplex, which was then further optimised. Optimisations included the amount of capture antibody coupled to magnetic microspheres, detection antibody concentration, incubation time and assay buffer matrix. Optimal antibody (capture and detection) concentrations are summarised in Table 1. The optimal assay buffer used was 81% distilled water, 10% Reagent diluent (R&D systems, UK) and 9% heat inactivated foetal calf serum (Gibco, UK). For the FMIA, 50μl of magnetic microspheres coupled with 20 μg/ml of capture antibody were first added to a 96 well, black, flat-bottomed plate and washed twice with wash buffer using a Bio-Plex Pro II Wash Station (Bio-Rad, UK). To this, 50 μl of prepared recombinant standards, unknown samples, controls or blanks (assay buffer only) were added. The plate was then incubated in the dark with shaking at RT for 2 h. To reduce bubbles from forming (and beads from sticking to sides) during incubation a high shaking setting (900–1100 rpm) was used for first 30 s then lower (300 rpm) for the rest of the incubation time. The plate was washed three times as before, then 100 μl of the detection antibody (in assay buffer) was added to the wells and the plate was incubated as before for 40 min. The plate was washed three times as previously, then 50 μl of diluted Streptavidin-PE solution (Bio-Rad) was added and the plate was incubated for a further 20 min. The plate was washed for a final three times, and then 125 μl of assay buffer was added. The plate was incubated with shaking for 5 min then the reaction was measured using a Bio-Plex 200® instrument and analysed with the Bio-Plex Manager software version 6.1. For details of measurements taken during the run see Hall et al. [1]. The instrument was calibrated daily and validated monthly using bead standards (Bio-Rad). Mean Fluorescent Intensity (MFI) for 100 microspheres corresponding to each individual cytokine analyte was recorded for each well. All reported MFI measurements were background corrected by the software (normalised) (F − Fo), where Fo was the background signal determined from the fluorescence measurement of the blank. Porcine brain samples were collected as part of a previous study and stored at −80 °C [4] and prepared using a modification of procedures described by Hulse et al. [4]. The hippocampus from the left hemisphere was removed from a brain slice of each pig (n = 14), weighed, crushed to a powder with liquid nitrogen and transferred to a 1.5 ml microtube. To this, 500 μl of cell lysis buffer (Bio-Rad, UK) with 1 μl stock solution was added and homogenised with a hand-held homogeniser (VWR VDI12). The total protein content was measured using Quick Start Bradford Protein Assay (Bio-Rad, UK) according to manufacturer’s instructions (Bio-Rad Quick start Bradford Assay) [5]. Brain extracts were frozen in aliquots (individually and equally pooled) at −80 °C pending FMIA analysis. Pooled extracts were spiked (with 4000 pg/ml) with both individual cytokines and a mixture of all six cytokines and then also diluted 2.5 fold, to validate the assay, ensuring recovery was always within 70–130% range.

Cell lysis buffer extraction involved [5] further synovial tissue samples homogenised in lysis buffer with protease inhibitors. Protease Inhibitor Cocktail lyophilised powder (Sigma-Aldrich, catalogue # P2714) was reconstituted with Tissue Extraction Reagent I (lysis buffer) (Invitrogen, catalogue # FNN0071) just before use. After reconstitution, the solution is stable for 24 h at 4 °C, therefore aliquots were made for immediate use and freezing. 0.1 g of tissue was weighed per sample and homogenised as in the above procedure in a final volume of 1 ml buffer. Homogenates were centrifuged at 5000 × g for 5 min (4 °C), according to the manufacturer’s instructions, and aliquoted and frozen as above.
Protein concentration of the all lysates was measured using a Bradford assay according to manufacturer’s instructions (Bio-Rad Quick start Bradford Assay) as before.
For hyaluronidase treatment we added 2 mg/ml hyaluronidase (sigma catalogue H3506) in 0.02 M PBS to the SF and incubated for 1 h at RT [10].

In an attempt to block antibodies and RF interference which can cause capture and detection antibodies to crosslink [8,11], a pooled SF sample was also incubated with a blocking buffer of either bovine plasma (Biosera) or a 1:1 equine and caprine serum (Sigma-Aldrich). Synovial fluid was incubated (1:1) for 30 min at RT before centrifuging at 1000 × g for 15 min.

steps.title: Activate and couple antibodies to magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Prepare magnetic carboxylated microspheres, activate their surface with EDC/S‑NHS, add recombinant cytokine protein (or capture antibody) for coupling, then block and store the coupled beads.

substeps.instruction: Bring all reagents to room temperature (RT).

Place 100 µl (1.25 × 10⁶) fluorescently distinct microspheres in a tube, separate from supernatant with a magnetic separator and wash once with 100 µl bead‑wash buffer; vortex 30 s, remove supernatant magnetically.
Resuspend washed beads in 80 µl bead‑activation buffer; vortex 30 s.
Add 10 µl S‑NHS (50 mg ml⁻¹, Fisher) and 10 µl EDC (50 mg ml⁻¹, Fisher) prepared in activation buffer; mix gently by vortexing.
Incubate in the dark with shaking for 20 min at RT.
Add 100 µl PBS (pH 7.4), vortex 10 s, remove supernatant magnetically; repeat PBS wash once more.
Resuspend beads in 100 µl PBS, vortex 30 s.
Add the recombinant cytokine protein (or capture antibody) to the activated beads, vortex to mix, and incubate 2 h in the dark at RT with shaking.
Remove supernatant magnetically, resuspend beads in 500 µl PBS.
Remove supernatant again, resuspend beads in 250 µl blocking buffer, vortex 15 s, and incubate 30 min in the dark at RT with shaking.
Remove supernatant, resuspend beads in 500 µl storage buffer.
Remove supernatant a final time and resuspend coupled beads in 150 µl storage buffer to obtain the desired concentration.
Determine bead concentration with an automated cell counter (TC10, Bio‑Rad).
Store coupled beads in the dark at 2–8 °C until use.

steps.title: Prepare assay buffer
steps.instruction: Make the optimal assay buffer consisting of 81 % distilled water, 10 % Reagent Diluent (R&D Systems) and 9 % heat‑inactivated foetal calf serum (Gibco).

steps.title: Run singleplex/multiplex FMIA on a 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Add magnetic beads, standards or samples, detection antibody, Streptavidin‑PE and assay buffer to a black flat‑bottom 96‑well plate, performing washes and incubations as specified, then read on a Bio‑Plex 200 instrument.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µl of magnetic beads (coupled with 20 µg ml⁻¹ capture antibody) to each well; wash twice with wash buffer using a Bio‑Plex Pro II Wash Station.
Add 50 µl of prepared recombinant standards, unknown samples, controls or blanks (assay buffer only) to the wells.
Incubate in the dark with shaking at RT for 2 h: shake at 900–1100 rpm for the first 30 s, then 300 rpm for the remaining time.
Wash wells three times as before.
Add 100 µl detection antibody (diluted in assay buffer) to each well; incubate in the dark with shaking at RT for 40 min (same shaking profile as above).
Wash wells three times.
Add 50 µl diluted Streptavidin‑PE (Bio‑Rad) to each well; incubate in the dark with shaking at RT for 20 min.
Wash wells three times.
Add 125 µl assay buffer to each well; incubate with shaking at RT for 5 min.
Read the plate on a Bio‑Plex 200® instrument; record mean fluorescent intensity (MFI) for 100 beads per cytokine.
Background‑correct MFI (F – F₀) using the software; generate a 5‑parameter logistic (5‑PL) standard curve; accept recoveries in the 70–130 % range.

steps.title: Validate assay – spike recovery
steps.instruction: Prepare spiked standards ranging from 10 000 to 40.06 pg ml⁻¹, run them in the FMIA, and calculate recovery; acceptable recovery is 70–130 %.

substeps.instruction: Add known amounts of each cytokine (10 000–40.06 pg ml⁻¹) to separate wells containing matrix (e.g., brain, placenta, synovial fluid).
Run the FMIA as described above.
Calculate % recovery = (measured concentration / expected concentration) × 100; accept only 70–130 %.

steps.title: Validate assay – repeatability
steps.instruction: Assess intra‑ and inter‑assay variation by running standards in triplicate over three days.

substeps.instruction: Intra‑assay: prepare seven recombinant cytokine standards, run each in triplicate within a single assay run; calculate coefficient of variation (CV).
Inter‑assay: prepare the same seven standards, run each in triplicate on three separate days; calculate CV across days.

steps.title: Validate assay – cross‑reactivity
steps.instruction: Test specificity by running wells that contain all capture antibodies and cytokine recombinants but only one detection antibody; calculate any non‑specific signal as % cross‑reactivity.

steps.title: Extract protein from porcine brain tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenise frozen brain tissue in cell‑lysis buffer, measure protein concentration, and store extracts at –80 °C.

substeps.instruction: Weigh hippocampus from left hemisphere of each brain slice; crush to powder with liquid nitrogen.
Transfer powder to a 1.5 ml microtube and add 500 µl cell‑lysis buffer (Bio‑Rad) containing 1 µl stock solution; homogenise with a hand‑held homogeniser (VWR VDI‑12).
Measure total protein using Quick‑Start Bradford assay (Bio‑Rad) according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Aliquot brain extracts and freeze at –80 °C until FMIA analysis.

steps.title: Prepare pooled and spiked brain/placenta dilutions
steps.instruction: Pool extracts, spike with cytokines (4000 pg ml⁻¹), and perform six 2.5‑fold serial dilutions.

substeps.instruction: Pool individual brain extracts (or placenta extracts) and create a pooled sample.
Spike pooled sample with 4000 pg ml⁻¹ of each cytokine (individual and a mixture of all six).
Serially dilute the pooled (spiked) sample six times using a 2.5‑fold dilution factor.
Calculate percentage recovery for each dilution.

steps.title: Extract protein from synovial tissue – RIPA method
steps.instruction: Homogenise ~0.3 g synovial tissue in 3 ml RIPA buffer, solubilise 2 h on ice, centrifuge and store lysate.

substeps.instruction: Weigh ~0.3 g synovial tissue; add 3 ml RIPA lysis buffer (Alpha Diagnostics #RIPA‑50 with protease/phosphatase inhibitors).
Homogenise on ice; let solubilise for 2 h on ice.
Centrifuge at 3000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C.
Transfer supernatant to a new cryovial; store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Extract protein from synovial tissue – cell‑lysis buffer method
steps.instruction: Homogenise 0.1 g tissue in 1 ml cell‑lysis buffer with freshly reconstituted protease inhibitor cocktail, centrifuge and store.

substeps.instruction: Reconstitute Protease Inhibitor Cocktail (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat #P2714) with Tissue Extraction Reagent I (Invitrogen, cat #FNN0071) just before use; keep aliquots on ice (stable 24 h at 4 °C).
Weigh 0.1 g synovial tissue; add 1 ml cell‑lysis buffer containing protease inhibitors; homogenise as above.
Centrifuge at 5000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aliquot supernatant and freeze at –80 °C.

steps.title: Extract protein from synovial tissue – PBS method
steps.instruction: Homogenise ~200 mg tissue in 2 ml PBS, perform freeze‑thaw cycles, centrifuge, and store supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Weigh ~200 mg synovial tissue; add 2 ml PBS (1×).
Homogenise on ice with hand‑held homogeniser (VWR VDI‑12).
Subject sample to two freeze‑thaw cycles.
Centrifuge at 5000 × g for 5 min; collect supernatant.
If fat globules remain, repeat centrifugation.
Aliquot supernatant and freeze at –80 °C.

steps.title: Measure protein concentration of synovial lysates
steps.instruction: Determine total protein in all synovial lysates using the Bio‑Rad Quick‑Start Bradford assay.

steps.title: Process pooled synovial fluid
steps.instruction: Centrifuge pooled synovial fluid at low speed and collect supernatant for FMIA.

substeps.instruction: Pool synovial fluid from four pigs.
Centrifuge at 1000 × g for 15 min.
Collect supernatant for downstream assays.

steps.title: Treat synovial fluid with hyaluronidase
steps.instruction: Add hyaluronidase to pooled synovial fluid and incubate for 1 h at RT.

substeps.instruction: Prepare hyaluronidase solution: 2 mg ml⁻¹ hyaluronidase (Sigma cat H3506) in 0.02 M PBS.
Add the solution to synovial fluid (final concentration 2 mg ml⁻¹).
Incubate 1 h at RT.

steps.title: Filter synovial fluid with Vivaspin columns
steps.instruction: Pass synovial fluid through 50 kDa MWCO Vivaspin 500 columns, centrifuge, and test spiked recovery before and after filtration.

substeps.instruction: Load synovial fluid onto Sartorius Vivaspin 500 (50 kDa MWCO, PES membrane) columns.
Centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 9 min.
Spike aliquots taken before (pre) and after (post) filtration with 4000 pg ml⁻¹ cytokine standards.
Prepare additional dilutions of 1:2, 1:5, 1:10, 1:20, 1:40 to assess dilution effects.

steps.title: Block antibodies and RF in synovial fluid
steps.instruction: Incubate synovial fluid with blocking serum, then centrifuge.

substeps.instruction: Mix pooled synovial fluid 1:1 with either bovine plasma (Biosera) or a 1:1 mixture of equine and caprine serum (Sigma‑Aldrich).
Incubate 30 min at RT.
Centrifuge at 1000 × g for 15 min; collect supernatant.

steps.title: Collect and process porcine blood plasma
steps.instruction: Draw blood into EDTA tubes, centrifuge, freeze plasma, pool samples, and prepare for FMIA.

substeps.instruction: Collect 6 ml blood from tail or ear vein into a 6 ml EDTA vacutainer (Henry Schein Animal Health).
Place tubes on ice and immediately transfer to a refrigerated centrifuge (4 °C).
Centrifuge 15 min at 1400 × g.
Aliquot plasma into four 1.5 ml pre‑labelled tubes; freeze at –80 °C.
On assay day, thaw pooled plasma on ice; create three pooled samples.
Analyse pooled plasma neat and diluted 1:2 for IL‑1β, IL‑6, TNF‑α.
Spike pooled plasma with cytokines at 4000 pg ml⁻¹ (high) and 640 pg ml⁻¹ (low); also dilute spiked samples 1:2 for recovery calculations.

steps.title: Run FMIA on tissue and plasma extracts
steps.instruction: Perform the FMIA (as in step 3) on all prepared extracts (brain, placenta, synovial tissue lysates, synovial fluid preparations, and plasma) using the appropriate dilution series and spike‑recovery controls.
